 9 M’sian doubles pairs advance in Hong Kong Open 
 9 M’sian doubles pairs advance in Hong Kong Open 
 18-Nov-2026, 23:44 18 Nov 2026, 23:44 K. Parkaran Share However, only one of the four Malaysian singles players survives.
 World No 9 duo Man Wei Chong-Tee Kai Wun took just 24 minutes to overcome their Thai opponents. (Bernama pic) 
 PETALING JAYA : Nine Malaysian doubles pairs across all categories advanced to the second round of the Hong Kong Open badminton championships today with victories in their opening matches. 
 However, only one of the four Malaysian singles players survived the first round of the World Tour Super 500 tournament being played at the Kai Tak Arena.
 In the men’s doubles, newly crowned Japan Masters champions Aaron Tai-Yap Roy King defeated the higher-ranked Taiwanese pair of Chiu Hsiang Chieh-Wang Chi Lin 21-17, 21-14 in a match lasting 29 minutes.
 Aaron-Roy King, playing in only their sixth tournament together, will face Indonesia’s world No 18 pair, Leo Rolly Carnando-Daniel Marthin, in the second round tomorrow.
 Man Wei Chong-Tee Kai Wun, ranked world No 9, were in complete control over Thailand’s world No 27 pair, Peeratchai Sukphun-Pakkapon Teeraratsakul, winning 21-10, 21-14 in just 24 minutes. They will face Taiwan’s He Zhe Wei-Huang Jui Hsuan next.
 However, world No 31 pair Nur Azriyn Ayub-Tan Wee Kiong were made to sweat in their tie against Japan’s 50th-ranked Haruki Kawabe-Kenta Matsukawa before winning 21-16, 17-21, 21-19 in 54 minutes.
 Their opponents in the second round will be Satwiksairaj Rankireddy-Chirag Shetty of India, ranked world No 6.
 Chia Wei Jie-Teo Ee Yi defeated South Korea’s Jin Yong-Jo Song Hyun 21-16, 18-21, 21-12 to book a last-16 clash with China’s world No 3 pair, Liang Wei Keng-Wang Chang.
 In the mixed doubles, three Malaysian pairs reached the second round.
 Leading the charge were world No 14 Hoo Pang Ron-Lai Pei Jing, who edged Indonesians Marwan Faza-Aisyah Salsabila Putri Pranata 21-14, 22-24, 21-13 in 52 minutes.
 They face a daunting task against China’s world No 2 pair Jiang Zhen Bang-Wei Ya Xin in the next round, having lost to them in straight games in their last two meetings.
 An uphill battle also awaits Wong Tien Ci-Lim Chiew Sien, who beat the Indian scratch pair of Hariharan Amsakarunan-Tanisha Crasto 28-26, 21-14 in 39 minutes. Their opponents in the next round are China’s world No 1 pair of Feng Yan Zhe-Huang Dong Ping.
 World No 12 pair Goh Soon Huat-Shevon Jemie Lai defeated Zhi Yi Chen-Francesca Corbett of the US 21-17, 21-14 in 29 minutes and will clash with another American pair, Presley Smith-Jennie Gai, in the second round.
 In the women’s doubles, Low Zi Yu-Noraqilah Maisarah Ramdan defeated Thailand’s Ornicha Jongsathapornparn-Sabrina Sophita Wedler 21-18, 21-16 in 35 minutes and will face Taiwan’s Hsu Yin Hui-Lin Jhih Yun tomorrow.
 Pearly Tan-M Thinaah, who won their opening round yesterday, will take on Hong Kong’s Yeung Nga Ting-Yeung Pui Lam next.
 Only women’s shuttler Wong Ling Ching reached the second round in the singles events when she defeated Ishika Jaiswal of the US 16-21, 21-17, 21-15 in 64 minutes. She will face Thai ace Ratchanok Intanon in the second round.
 K Letshanaa lost to Indonesian Putri Kusuma Wardini 15-21, 12-21 in 37 minutes.
 In men’s singles, Cheam June Wei lost to world No 3 Anders Antonsen 15-21, 14-21 in 38 minutes, while Leong Jun Hao lost to China’s Dong Tian Yao 12-21, 13-21 in 34 minutes.
